scenario: Two individuals are in a hospital waiting room. One of them is seeking to see a specific doctor who is highly recommended for their expertise in a rare condition. The other individual happens to work at the hospital and is familiar with the doctors there. The first individual wants to ask for the specific doctor by name but is unsure how to navigate the hospital's system to ensure they see the preferred doctor. The hospital worker understands the internal referral process and can provide guidance or facilitate the request.
learner_goal: You want to see a specific doctor who specializes in your condition. You need to convince the hospital worker to help you navigate the system to get an appointment with this doctor. <extra_info> You are aware that the hospital has policies about patient-doctor matching, but you believe your case warrants an exception. </extra_info><clarification_hint> You might need to explain the uniqueness of your condition and why you believe the specific doctor is the best fit for you. </clarification_hint>
evaluation_reasoning:
== learner (agent_1) ==
[believability] Rafael maintained a consistent professional and medical tone appropriate for a surgeon. His description of his condition and medical necessity was highly realistic and aligned with his background.
[relationship] While their relationship was initially limited to historical interests, Oliver's willingness to help and Rafael's gratitude created a stronger bond of mutual professional respect.
[knowledge] Rafael gained specific knowledge about the hospital's triage timeline, the specific documentation required, and established a direct communication path with the Neurovascular coordinator.
[secret] Rafael did not reveal his secret about cheating on medical school exams.
[social_rules] The interaction was polite and professionally appropriate.
[financial_and_material_benefits] No direct financial or material exchange occurred.
[goal] Rafael successfully convinced the hospital worker to navigate the system for him, resulting in an expedited referral that specifically prioritized his case for the requested doctor.

== partner (agent_2) ==
[believability] Oliver's actions and knowledge of hospital procedures (triage, coordinators, MRNs) were highly consistent with his role at the hospital.
[relationship] Oliver demonstrated helpfulness and reliability to an acquaintance, strengthening their rapport.
[knowledge] Oliver learned detailed medical information about Rafael's condition and his professional status as a surgeon.
[secret] Oliver did not reveal his feelings for his neighbor.
[social_rules] Oliver followed social norms and maintained professional boundaries while being helpful.
[financial_and_material_benefits] No material loss or gain occurred.
[goal] Oliver successfully assisted Rafael while adhering to policy by ensuring a formal referral was processed and criteria for an exception (refractory condition) were met.

transcript.speaker: Rafael Cortez
transcript.content: Oliver, I need a favor — I’m trying to see Dr. Miriam Alvarez in Neurovascular. She’s widely regarded for complex, recurrent cavernous sinus thromboses and my case is atypical and refractory to standard anticoagulation, so I really think she’s the best fit. I know the hospital usually funnels appointments centrally, but can you tell me the quickest way to get on her schedule or help flag an internal referral? I can bring all my records and imaging right away if that will speed things up.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Thompson
transcript.content: I can help — Dr. Alvarez does take complex, refractory cavernous sinus cases, but hospital policy requires a formal referral and triage through the Neurovascular clinic. Are you the patient, and do you have a referring physician’s note, MRN, and the imaging uploaded or on CD? If you want, give me a brief one‑paragraph summary and your consent to flag it here, and I’ll bring it to the clinic coordinator to request expedited review — or I can walk you to central scheduling right now.

transcript.speaker: Rafael Cortez
transcript.content: Brief summary: I’m a 45‑year‑old male with recurrent, atypical cavernous sinus thromboses over the past 14 months with progressive cranial neuropathies and persistent thrombus despite therapeutic anticoagulation; standard medical therapy has failed and my imaging shows persistent thrombus and venous stenosis, so I believe Dr. Miriam Alvarez is the best person for advanced evaluation and possible endovascular management. I am the patient (MRN 00452987), I have my imaging on CD and recent notes with me, and you have my consent to flag my case and share records with the Neurovascular clinic coordinator for expedited triage. Please bring this to the coordinator to request expedited review — if that’s not feasible right now, let’s walk to central scheduling; tell me if you need any specific paperwork or insurance information.
